scope: Proposition 4.3 (Coordinate heights and local norms) of the manuscript “Quaternionic division points on curves in the Siegel threefold” (preprints/Quaternionic-Division-Points-on-Curves-in-the-Siegel-Threefold-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 016 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e11b4b068502ced9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Choose the vectors of Proposition 4.2. Their affine coordinates in the fixed frame satisfy h(z(t), a, P) ≤ C(h + log d). (4.2) There are center neighborhoods at every place, with a single integral description outside a fixed finite set of rational primes, such that for any selected weighted set V on the actual center branches, X v∈V wv log max(1, ∥z(t), P∥v) ≤ C(1 + log h + log d). (4.3) These statements hold for the finitely many conjugate fixed charts. They also hold after a bounded denominator and a polarized isogeny of any one fixed multiplier are applied to the vectors.
